## Terminal

```{.bash filename="Terminal"}
quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in this directory.

Quarto's Typst output has no list of listings, no alternative text for a formula, no appendix that works outside a book, and no watermark.
You can write the Typst for each one, but you then copy it into every project and keep it in step with your template.
Typst Extras does this in one filter, and it works with Quarto's default Typst format, with Typst books and with third-party Typst templates.

## Quick start

Add the filter and set the options in the front matter of the document:

```yaml
format: typst
filters:
  - typst-extras
extensions:
  typst-extras:
    list-of: true
    watermark: "DRAFT"
```

Then write the document as usual.
The render adds a list of every figure, table and listing at the start of the body.
It also draws the grey text `DRAFT` on every page.
To move a section to the end as an appendix, put the class `.appendix` on its level-1 heading:

```markdown
# Extra results {.appendix}
```

The heading then reads `Appendix A` followed by the title, and the figures in the section read `Figure A.1`.

See the [Reference](reference.qmd) for every option, and the [Examples](examples.qmd) for each of them rendered.

## Where it works

Every module acts on Typst output only.
In other formats, the document stays as it is, except that the `alt` attribute on a formula is removed.
The extension needs Quarto 1.11.9 or newer.
